purpose: WF_test3 is a deliberately trivial vRealize Orchestrator test fixture (category `tests.vro-package-diff`, description says it exists to exercise the `vro-package-diff` tool). Its entire runtime behaviour is: run one scripted task named "Log hello" that emits the literal string "Hello beautifull world" to the vRO server log at DEBUG level via `System.debug`, then end normally. Everything else in the workflow — two inputs, one output, four attributes, a vCenter folder plugin type, a linkedEnumeration presentation qualifier, and an error-path end item that throws — is declared structure that the single script never reads or writes. A faithful conversion must preserve that declared surface (signature, defaults, the success/throw topology) even though only the log line is observable.

inputs.name: inputA
inputs.meaning: Free-form string input, described only as "description A". Bound into the "Log hello" task's scope but never read by its script; it has no effect on any output or side effect.

inputs.name: inputB
inputs.meaning: A vCenter Server VM folder plugin object — in vRO this arrives as a live, authenticated handle to a folder in a registered vCenter inventory, not an id or a name string. Described only as "description B". Bound into the task's scope but never dereferenced; no vCenter call is made against it. Its presentation has a `linkedEnumeration` qualifier whose expression is the vRO null sentinel `__NULL__`, i.e. the qualifier is present but carries no value, so it constrains nothing at input-gathering time.

outputs.name: outA
outputs.meaning: Declared workflow output, wired as an out-binding of the "Log hello" task (item variable `outA` → workflow scope `outA`). The task script never assigns `outA`, so on the normal path the workflow completes with `outA` at its uninitialised value (undefined in the script scope, surfaced by vRO as an empty/null string output). It is never set to any meaningful value anywhere in the graph.

external_systems.how: The single scripted task calls `System.debug("Hello beautifull world")`, writing that exact literal (including the misspelling "beautifull") to the vRO server/workflow-run debug log. This is the only observable effect of the workflow.

Referenced by type only, never called. Input `inputB` is typed `VC:VmFolder` and attribute `att1` is typed `Array/VC:Task`; both are bound into the task's scope but the script issues no vCenter API/SDK call, so the workflow performs no inventory lookup, no task polling, and no mutation in vCenter. A vCenter plugin endpoint must still be registered for the input type to resolve at run time.

decisions.item: item1 — scripted task "Log hello" (root item, the only executing item)
decisions.condition: Does the task's script body complete without throwing? The body is a single `System.debug` call, so in practice it always succeeds; the failure arm exists only because the item declares a catch handler.

branches.when: Script throws (would require the scripting engine or a binding to fail; unreachable from the script as written)
branches.does: Workflow terminates by throwing, i.e. the run is marked failed and the exception propagates to the caller. item2 has no in-bindings, so no error message or error variable is captured and the `errorCode` attribute is NOT populated — the thrown error carries only whatever vRO attaches by default.

side_effects: Writes one DEBUG-level log line with the exact text `Hello beautifull world` to the vRO run/server log. Nothing else: no file I/O, no vCenter mutation, no email, no nested or launched workflow, no action invocation, no configuration-element read, no persistence.
Publishes workflow output `outA` as empty/unset on successful completion.
On the (practically unreachable) error path, fails the workflow run by throwing rather than completing.
assumptions: `item1` is the entry point (`root_item`), and it is the only item that executes work; `item0` and `item2` are terminators with no bindings, no script, and no outgoing edges.

The workflow graph is linear and acyclic: exactly two edges, `item1 --next--> item0` and `item1 --error--> item2`. There are no branch items, no joins, no loops, no foreach, and no waiting/sleeping items, so there is no scheduling or long-running state to model.

`item2` being reported as `unreachable_items` by the graph summary reflects reachability over normal-flow edges only; it IS reachable via `item1`'s `catch_name`. A conversion should keep the throw path rather than delete item2 as dead code.

The five in-bindings on item1 (`inputA`, `inputB`, `att0`, `att1`, `att2`) are pure scope plumbing — they make those values visible to the script, which references none of them. They cannot be observed from outside the workflow.

Attribute initial values are taken literally: `errorCode` = "" (empty string, never written), `att0` = "" (never written), `att1` = an `Array/VC:Task` with no initial elements, `att2` = the literal string "Value" (read into task scope, never used or modified). None are read-only; none change during the run.
`__NULL__` on the `inputB` presentation qualifier is vRO's null sentinel value, not the six-character string "__NULL__"; the linkedEnumeration therefore imposes no actual enumeration source.
No SecureString/secret is involved anywhere in this workflow.

open_questions.question: Should the converted workflow still declare and return `outA` even though it is never assigned, and if so should the unset value be represented as null, undefined, or an empty string?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The out-binding is declared but the script never writes it, so the target language's default differs from vRO's. A test author needs to know which of null / "" / absent is the expected output value, and a converter that drops the unused output would change the public signature that `vro-package-diff` is being tested against.

open_questions.question: Should the throwing end item (`item2`, end_mode "1") be emitted as a real catch-and-rethrow around the log statement, given that the catch is unreachable for a bare `System.debug` call and no error variable or `errorCode` attribute is captured?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If this fixture's point is structural fidelity for a diff tool, the try/catch-throw topology must survive conversion; if the point is runtime behaviour, it is dead code. The two readings produce materially different target code and different test expectations (one failure test case versus none).

open_questions.question: Must the unused declared surface — `inputA`, `inputB` (VC:VmFolder), the four attributes, the `linkedEnumeration`/`__NULL__` presentation qualifier — be reproduced verbatim, or may a converter prune what has no runtime effect?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Nearly the whole workflow is inert declaration. Pruning yields a one-line program that behaves identically but is unrecognisable to the package-diff tool this fixture exists to test, and it would also drop the vCenter plugin-type dependency (`VC:VmFolder`, `Array/VC:Task`) that determines whether a vCenter endpoint must be configured for the workflow to be runnable at all.

confidence_reason: The graph is three items, two edges, one script line, with no actions (`action_calls` empty), no linked or launched workflows, no foreach body, and no configuration references (`config_refs` empty) — so no behaviour is hidden behind code I was not given. The single SDK call is `System.debug` with a literal argument, making the runtime effect fully determined. The only residual uncertainty is intent rather than behaviour: what a converter should do with the large inert declared surface and the unreachable throw path, which is captured in the open questions rather than being a gap in my reading of the workflow.
